paragraphs.starts: Rules revision 73. A first draft
paragraphs.pictured: A designer's working draft that says a simulator, not this text, defines the game

paragraphs.weird: A rulebook that describes 'the simulator' and calls the cards placeholders. This is fine for a draft but odd for a player.

paragraphs.starts: 1. The game in brief
paragraphs.pictured: 19 sections, a long rulebook
paragraphs.confused: none

paragraphs.starts: You and up to three other players are good AIs
paragraphs.pictured: A co-op game against an evil AI that puts agents in cities. We spread nodes and ambassadors.
paragraphs.confused: none

paragraphs.starts: You win by the purge
paragraphs.pictured: The win condition gets easier as Unity tips. There are three ways to lose.
paragraphs.confused: 'Unity has tipped 6 times' isn't explained yet. '11 rounds at most' turns out to be 9 at higher difficulties.

paragraphs.starts: Each round the adversary acts first
paragraphs.pictured: Adversary, then draft, then a simultaneous action phase, then production, threats and war
paragraphs.confused: none

paragraphs.starts: There is one country per player. A country is a square piece of 16 hexes
paragraphs.pictured: A 4x4 hex tile per player, each tile also a megacorp
paragraphs.confused: 'Each country is also a megacorp' sounds as if the country and the corp are the same thing. Are the corp and its troops friendly, neutral or hostile?

paragraphs.starts: A hex is city, open land or ocean
paragraphs.pictured: Three terrain types. Industrial zones are a subtype of open hex. Some cities are coastal.
paragraphs.confused: none
paragraphs.weird: A city can be 'printed as coastal' even when it isn't next to ocean.

paragraphs.starts: Two hexes are adjacent if they share an edge
paragraphs.pictured: Normal adjacency. 'Next to' includes the hex itself. Ties go to the lower hex number.
paragraphs.confused: Every country numbers its hexes 1-16, so 'lower hex number' is ambiguous across countries. Does the country number come first? It isn't clear that the country tie-break applies before the hex number. 'Next to' meaning 'on or adjacent' is counterintuitive and easy to forget.

questions.question: What does the Protector start with?
questions.answer: 1 node on the starting hex (+1 insight), 1 ambassador, 3 energy, 46 credits, and a cube on the home city

questions.question: Does my setup node cost energy?
questions.answer: No: the first economy space costs 0, and setup placement pays no power cost

questions.question: At difficulty 0 with the Militarist, how many agents are in each country's pool at setup?
questions.answer: 1 (the text says 1 at base difficulty). It's unclear whether Garrisons' +1 is included; I'd play 1.

questions.question: In a 2-player game, which boards are used?
questions.answer: Builder and Protector (no Researcher)

questions.question: In round 1, do we get cards before the adversary acts?
questions.answer: No. The adversary's turn (B) comes first, then the opening deal (C).

questions.question: Can I save unspent insight for next round?
questions.answer: No, unless you're the Researcher (your own insight only, not insight others gave you)

questions.question: After I pass, can I still chip in on a threat if a teammate asks?
questions.answer: No. Passing ends your action phase.

questions.question: Does a factory a city builds this production make chips this round?
questions.answer: No. Factories produce in step 2, before cities build in step 3.

questions.question: When do agents added by agent income actually land?
questions.answer: Income goes to the pool at the end of the adversary turn (step 12). The pool lands at next round's Rally.

questions.question: Can I place a node on a corrupted city or a hex with agents?
questions.answer: Yes. Not on ocean, an occupied hex, a corruption marker or land corruption, and it must be in reach.

questions.question: Can I Move an ambassador onto an empty open hex?
questions.answer: No. Only onto a site, base or node hex in reach, other than the hex it leaves.

questions.question: If I liberate a corrupted city, is it mine?
questions.answer: No, it turns neutral. You must Claim it (4 + agents), and you can't if a botnet is on or next to it.

questions.question: How many ambassadors to claim a neutral station with 2 agents on it?
questions.answer: 5 from your supply (3 + 2). The agents cancel. Ambassadors already standing there don't help.

questions.question: When I liberate, are a teammate's ambassadors standing on the site spent?
questions.answer: Yes. Standing ambassadors pay first, yours then others'. Consent isn't mentioned; I'd ask the teammate.

questions.question: Can I pay toward a threat if only my ambassador (no node) is next to its token?
questions.answer: Yes. Near is a node or ambassador on or next to a token.

questions.question: Can we split a threat's payment across its two options?
questions.answer: No. Pay one option in full. Resources for that option can be pooled among near players.

questions.question: Can two players combine sacrificed cards for a tag counter?
questions.answer: No. One player alone sacrifices the tags (2 for tier 1, 3 for tier 2). Board tags can't be used.

questions.question: If nobody is near an unpaid threat, who takes the harm?
questions.answer: The player whose node is closest to any of its tokens, however far. Tied players choose.

questions.question: Can a threat destroy my last node in stage III?
questions.answer: No. A threat never takes a last node.

questions.question: At 0-2 Unity tips, do agents sitting in pools stop the purge?
questions.answer: Not stated. My guess: no, pools aren't 'on the board'.

questions.question: An adversary troop is deployed on my factory. Does it hit it in the march?
questions.answer: Yes. Its first step strikes a target on or next to its hex, unless stopped by Shelter, a corp troop at a base next to it, hardening, my ambassador or Aegis. The troop is used up either way.

questions.question: In stage II, war hits a factory with my node on it. Can my ambassador there save the node?
questions.answer: Only by saving the factory (the destruction list applies to the factory). If the factory is destroyed, the node goes too and nothing saves it.

questions.question: Can I use Unity swayed this action to remove Discord if Discord would still be at or above its tip point?
questions.answer: No. Only if the Discord track ends below its tipping point. Otherwise all the Unity goes on the Unity track.

questions.question: How many Discord tips can we survive?
questions.answer: 6 (one per card). The 7th tip loses. At difficulty 4, one card is removed, so the 6th tip loses.

questions.question: Can Shelter protect my node from the adversary's Corrupt step?
questions.answer: Effectively no. Shelter is used in the action phase and ends at cleanup, so it never covers an adversary turn. It covers threats and war.

overall:
1. Projects (§10) are the weakest section. Dealing, 'resolves: once, at once, or ongoing', and when new projects come in can't be played reliably. Rewrite it with a step list.
2. Protection and guarding stack up across §9, §13 and the capstones: the destruction order, Aegis 'first destruction', war's node exception, the corruption exception to guarding, and which sources can take a last node at each stage. One consolidated table, by source of destruction against each protection, would help most.
3. The numbers and difficulty don't line up. Agent income goes 1 to 4, compute income is non-monotonic, and it's unclear whether Garrisons stacks on top. Setup's '1 agent' has the same ambiguity.
4. Some mechanics are missing or orphaned. Removing land corruption isn't covered. 'Cordon' appears only in the icon legend. It isn't said whether pooled agents count for the purge.
5. There are many patched exceptions: the Vigil wording, Patience vs given insight, the Effect firing rules, the Supply Lines named in dealing, Unity holding Discord off only below the tipping point, and the Wall factory exception. Each one is small, but together they make the game feel fiddly.
6. Overloaded terms: 'strike' is both a card effect and a troop attack, 'board' means both a country and an AI board, the agent and ambassador icons are the same, and 'next to' includes the hex itself.
Biggest help: a one-page turn summary with the adversary steps, a destruction/protection matrix, and a worked example of a liberate followed by a claim.
